entities.title: Arson and attacks on state buildings, 9 September 2025

properties.summary: Second day of unrest. Protesters set fire to the Federal Parliament, Singha Durbar, the Supreme Court and the presidential residence Shital Niwas, attacked the Kantipur complex and homes of political leaders, and prisons were attacked. HRW says arson continued until about 10 p.m., when the army was deployed.

evidence.note: Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.
Individual sub-events carry their own verification.

entities.title: Police order to use necessary force ('Peter 1')

properties.summary: According to police radio logs reported by the BBC, a call sign 'Peter 1', identified as IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, told officers to use necessary force at 12:40, ten minutes after the curfew. The report says a second order followed at 12:41 from the operations in-charge. AFP adds that police said Khapung acted after authorisation from a government security committee headed by a senior civil servant.

evidence.note: 12:40 is given by the Ratopati report of the BBC investigation; News24/AFP says '10 minutes after a curfew had come into effect'; the curfew started at 12:30 per other outlets.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.
Every copy goes back to the single BBC investigation.

entities.title: Parliament gate vandalised and set on fire

properties.summary: Protesters vandalised the Parliament gate in New Baneshwar and, per Setopati, set the main gate on fire.

evidence.note: Setopati posted at 15:17 and 15:47 on 8 September; the posting time is not the time of the fire.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.
Arson of the gate is reported by Setopati; ANI says only 'vandalised'.

entities.title: Attacks on leaders' homes and party offices

properties.summary: On 9 September protesters set fire to the residences of prominent politicians and entered the office of Nepal's largest party (Al Jazeera); Newschecker reports the house of communication minister Prithvi Subba Gurung in Lalitpur was targeted. Locations are neighbourhood level only.

evidence.note: Al Jazeera live-blog entry stamped 11:50 GMT (17:35 Nepal time); posting time only.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.

entities.title: Federal Parliament building set on fire

properties.summary: Protesters broke into the Parliament premises and set the main building on fire on 9 September; Reuters reports army firefighters fighting a blaze in the main hall the next day.

evidence.note: Hour not stated by the sources retrieved. Al Jazeera live blog entry 12:00 GMT (17:45 Nepal time) is a posting time.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.

entities.title: Singha Durbar set on fire

properties.summary: Protesters entered Singha Durbar through its western gate on 9 September and set the main administrative complex ablaze.

evidence.note: Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.

entities.title: Supreme Court building set on fire

properties.summary: The Supreme Court building was torched on 9 September. HRW places it shortly after the attack on Kantipur Television; the court later worked from a tent on its premises.

evidence.note: Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.

entities.title: Kantipur complex attacked

properties.summary: HRW says 10 to 15 men with sticks, knives and gasoline vandalised the Kantipur Television headquarters between 1:30 and 2 p.m. on 9 September. Al Jazeera's live blog reports protesters setting fire to a building housing Kantipur Publications, in an entry stamped 12:50 GMT (18:35 Nepal time).

evidence.note: HRW window 13:30 to 14:00. The Al Jazeera entry stamp converts to 18:35 Nepal time; the gap may be live-blog lag, or two separate attacks (vandalism, then fire). The sources do not settle it.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.
Two time accounts that do not match.

entities.title: Shital Niwas set on fire

evidence.note: 'By 4:25 p.m.' is an upper bound for when the fire was seen.

entities.title: Army deployed as arson ends

entities.title: Army takes control of Kathmandu

properties.summary: Armed soldiers took control of Kathmandu on 10 September, ordering residents indoors under an indefinite curfew; soldiers guarded Parliament while army firefighters worked on the main hall.

entities.title: Prison breaks

properties.summary: Prisons were attacked on 9 September. HRW says thousands of prisoners were freed; Fox News reports that two prisons in western Nepal were stormed with nearly 900 escapes; the commission report as summarised by Ratopati gives 14,555 inmates escaped from various prisons.

evidence.note: Date as in HRW's account of 9 September.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.

entities.title: Commission report on Bhadra 23 and 24 incidents

properties.summary: Commission of inquiry report on the 8 and 9 September events, reported as under cabinet review on 9 March 2026. evidence.note: Month precision: sources give publication dates (9 and 26 March 2026), not the submission date.
Classification by the dataset from the cited reporting.
Key findings reach this dataset through Ratopati's summary, not the report text.
